name: Fixed-size sliding window
whenToUse: The standard answer: one pass, a running sum, no extra memory.

card.signals: "contiguous subarray", "length is equal to k" (the window size never changes) and "maximum average". Two neighbouring windows share k − 1 elements, so most of the work is the same.
card.pattern: a fixed-size window. Build the first window of k elements, then slide it one step at a time: one element enters on the right, one leaves on the left. Each element is added once and dropped once, so the scan is O(n).
card.coreIdea: keep total, the sum of the window. Sliding costs two operations: total += nums[right], total -= nums[left]. All windows have length k, so compare sums and divide by k only once, at the end.

invariant: After each slide, the window nums[left..right] has exactly k elements, and total is their sum.
